name: boot-progression
symbols_from_why: Runs against the PINNED BASE ROM: every symbol it reads is vanilla.
description: Re-implements pokemon/tools/boot_proof.py's three hardcoded gMain assertions as a spec, proving the generic harness reproduces what Slice 0 hardcoded -- plus a pointer-chase (deref) probe that resolves the CURRENT callback and reads its first THUMB halfword out of ROM.

probes.why: gMain.vblankCounter1 (include/main.h offset 0x20). Incremented by the VBlank IRQ handler, so a rising value proves the ROM executes its main loop rather than sitting black-screened or spinning in the BIOS.
gMain.callback2 (offset 0x04). A function pointer; resolving it against pokeemerald.sym names the screen the engine is on.
gMain.state (offset 0x438), the sub-state counter inside the current callback. Sampled to show a u8 probe reads the low byte only, not a neighbour.

THE POINTER-CHASE PROBE. deref: read the pointer at gMain+4 on EVERY sample (never cached), then read the halfword it points AT. This is mechanically identical to the gSaveBlock1Ptr/gSaveBlock2Ptr chase doc 44 requires, but its target is valid at boot, so the mechanism can be proven before a save state exists. Not sampled at frame 1: callback2 is legitimately NULL before the engine installs its first callback.

gSaveBlock2Ptr itself, read as a pointer and resolved back to a name. Doc 44: this is re-rolled at every battle start and map load, so a harness that caches it is wrong. Asserted here only for the property that holds at boot -- see sb2_first_bytes.

A deref THROUGH gSaveBlock2Ptr: the exact saveblock access path Slice 2 needs. At boot there is no save loaded, so no assertion is made about the CONTENT; what is asserted is that the chase itself lands somewhere readable and inside gSaveblock2's storage. The mechanism is what this probe proves.

assert.why: boot_proof.py assertion 1: the engine is alive.
boot_proof.py assertion 2: every non-null callback2 is a real symbol. Zero is allowed because the engine has legitimately not installed a callback at frame 1.
...but by the end it must not be null; a null callback late means the engine lost its callback.

boot_proof.py assertion 3, strengthened: the boot state machine visited at least three distinct screens rather than hanging on one. This is the assertion a 'the .gba file exists' check sails straight past.
The exact progression doc 54 §3 observed, now asserted by name and in order rather than merely counted.
Every pointer chase landed on readable memory.
The re-read pointer resolves to a real function every time.
The chase followed the callback as it MOVED -- the same progression as the direct probe, reached by dereferencing rather than by reading a fixed address. A cached pointer could not produce this.
The dereferenced target contains actual THUMB code, not zeros: the chase reached ROM, not an unmapped hole.

The saveblock pointer is NOT a constant across a single run, which is the whole reason a deref probe must re-read it every sample instead of caching it (doc 44). One change is the robust floor: it is null at frame 1 and non-null later. Look at the printed sample table for the stronger, un-asserted observation -- the pointer also MOVES within gSaveblock2 mid-run (0200b9b0 -> 0200ba24 = the +0x74 ASLR offset). That second change is deliberately not asserted: it depends on where the engine happens to re-roll during boot, and a fragile assertion is worse than an honest observation.
The saveblock pointer points into gSaveblock2's storage -- resolving an observed POINTER VALUE back to a symbol name, the mechanism every later saveblock probe depends on.
The saveblock pointer chase lands on readable memory on every sample. No claim is made about the bytes: no save is loaded at boot.
